newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Delicate talks to free Western hostages in Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Delicate talks to free Western hostages in Nigeria.

text.p: Delicate negotiations were in progress on Thursday to try to free 20 foreigners held hostage on a barge by Nigerians demanding work, officials of the company at the centre of the crisis said.
However, a Nigerian military government statement from the capital Abuja on Thursday said no foreigners had been taken hostage.
"A group of unemployed youths who have been protesting marginalisation by an oil industry company, Globe Star, in its employment policy went on rampage and seized the company's barge," it said.
The statement said the barge had been released following intervention by security agents, adding ... "no oil rig or foreign nationals were involved in the incident."

The Nigerian statement contradicts information on the incident by Western diplomats and officials of the French oil contracting firm ETPM, which is going through its second hostage-taking in Nigeria since December.

"We are still talking. It is very delicate negotiations," said an ETPM official about the negotiations to free the 16 Frenchmen, three Britons and an American held on company barge DLB1 by about 70 local people demanding employment.
Other sources said the locals, some of whom also work for ETPM, wanted better conditions of services.
Western diplomats from the nations involved said the hostages had not been harmed.
"We didn't get any information that the hostages are in bad shape so we think they are reasonably all right," one said.
ETPM went through a similar crisis last Christmas when 28 of its foreign workers including 10 Filipinos and nine Frenchmen were held on a barge offshore by 60 Nigerian workers demanding higher wages.
Apart from being deprived of food for two of the five days they were held captive, the hostages were not harmed.
The latest crisis began on Tuesday when the local workers seized the barge with the foreigners on board in the Escravos area off the western oil coastal town of Warri.
The barge beached on Wednesday near Warri, Lagos diplomats said.
The French embassy in Lagos was in touch with ETPM and monitoring the negotiations between the French company and the villagers on the situation, they said.
French company Lyonnaise des Eaux-Dumez said in Paris that ETPM was a joint venture between it and McDermott International Inc MRD.N.
ETPM spokeswoman in Paris, Ariane Malzac, told French television the problem was linked to rivalries between local groups.
"It's an inter-community problem...The people we employ are very well-paid. The other communities know this. They would also like to be paid by us," she said.
Communities in oil-producing areas have long been restive over lack of modern amenities in regions responsible for Nigeria's oil wealth. Clashes with oil companies have been common.
